old_title: England v Sri Lanka: men's tri-series cricket one-day international - live
new_title: Sri Lanka stun England by chasing down 430 to win as ODI records tumble - as it happened
old_text:
46th over: England 362-3 (Brook 168, Jacks 35) Brook uses his rubber wrists to whip Fernando behind square on the leg side for four. Yeah, fours are good but languid sixes down the ground are better. Brook launches his eighth six before taking a single to keep strike.
Wherever he is in the world, I hope Kevin Pietersen is watching this.
"I do remember the 1979 World Cup final, I'm afraid," says John Stedman. "Wasn't that the one when Clive Lloyd, one of the finest fielders to have ever played the game dropped Geoff Boycott, with disastrous consequences - for England?"
In defence of Sir Geoffrey, England would have lost that game 10 times out of 10 once West Indies reached 286-9. (Also, it was Beefy who encouraged Boycott and Mike Brearley to continue at the same tempo, but that's another story.)
45th over: England 351-3 (Brook 158, Jacks 34) Brook deliberately opens the face to slice an attempted wide yorker Malinga over short third for six. I mean, why wouldn't you? It's the oldest shot in the book.
Sri Lanka, their collective brain utterly fried, waste their last review when Jacks chased a wide yorker and is beaten.
Five overs remaining, 25 needed for Brook to beat Stokes' record.
"Hello Rob," writes Krishnamoorthy V. "Should we change the name from Brook to Flood or Torrent?"
44th over: England 338-3 (Brook 151, Jacks 29) Fernando knocks Brook off his feet with a terrific yorker outside off stump. Brook dusts himself down and responds with the jauntiest of reverse laps for four.
Fernando nails another yorker to make ittwo dot balls in three, so Brook charges his next delivery and slashes it deliberately for four. Brook's skill, audacity and imagination often overshadow the brilliance of his placement.
Oh good lord, stop this now. Brook moves past 150 with a reverse lap over short third for yet another boundary. He's 151 not out from 97 balls, with 16 fours and seven sixes. Oh, and at one stage he was 13 from 24.
When Brook plays like this, he makes Stick Cricket look like a 1960s Ashes Test.
43rd over: England 323-3 (Brook 138, Jacks 29) Brook scoops Malinga for his seventh six. Yawn, another six. A single down the ground takes him past his previous ODI best, a coruscating 136* (from 66 balls) against Sri Lanka in January.
If Brook wasn't batting like Stan McCabe circa 1938, we'd be raving about Will Jacks' innings. He flicks four more and has raced to 29 from 12 balls. Sri Lanka - who won the toss, remember - are in a world of pain.
Sri Lanka's fifth bowler, a combination of Shanaka, Kamindu Mendis and Liyanage, has figures of 8-0-83-0. If you're an England fan who remembers the 1979 World Cup final, you have permission to wince.
42nd over: England 309-3 (Brook 130, Jacks 24) Sri Lanka are haemorrhaging boundaries. Jacks larrups three in four deliveries off Madushanka - don't ask me to describe them, I can't keep up - in an over that costs 16. Never mind 350; England will want at least 400 from this position.
41st over: England 293-3 (Brook 129, Jacks 9) Brook shapes to ramp Shanaka, who bowls a low full toss well wide of off stump. Brook adjusts his hands and tickles it past short third and away to the boundary. That's absolu... is that even legal? It's an extraordinary shot.
And that's just for starters. Brook flips six over square leg, panels four over extra cover and smears a straight hit for four more. Twenty from the over.
I vividly recall standing at a bus stop in Orkney in the summer of 2018, listening to a Test Match Special podcast, when Michael Vaughan said there was a kid at Yorkshire who would play for England. I'd never heard of Harry Brook, but Vaughan spoke with such certainty that I made a point of following his career. In the next two seasons he averaged 25 and 21 in first-class cricket, and I thought Vaughany has sold us a pup. Wrong!
40th over: England 273-3 (Brook 109, Jacks 9) Brook repeats the ramp stroke next ball. A rattled Fernando bowls a front-foot no-ball and, though England can't take advantage of the free hit, it's another big over: 14 from it.
Brook ramps Asitha Fernando for four to reach another magnificent century: 75 balls, nine fours, five sixes. It's his fourth hundred in ODIs, all as captain. He was 13 not out from 24 balls, which means he's hit 88 from the last 51.
39th over: England 259-3 (Brook 97, Jacks 8) An utterly brilliant stroke from Brook, who steers a near-perfect wide yorker from Madushanka for four. He did that a few times during the Hundred as well. First they came for the yorker, these batting geniuses; now they're going after the wide yorker. No delivery is safe.
Jacks bullies his first boundary to make it 11 from the over. Never mind 300; England will want at least 350 from this position.
38th over: England 248-3 (Brook 92, Jacks 2) Will Jacks, the best finisher in this England team, is promoted to No5. Another good over from Asitha Fernando, who has become a pretty reliable attack leader for Sri Lanka. His figures today are 7-1-29-1. Yep, one: a maiden.
WICKET! England 244-3 (Root c Wellalage b Fernando 69)
Root tries to chip Asitha Fernando over the leg side and spoons a simple catch to midwicket. He'll be annoyed to miss out on a century but he's given England a superb platform with a quietly charming innings of 69 from 66 balls.
37th over: England 244-2 (Root 69, Brook 90) Brook manhandles Malinga back over his head and away to the boundary. Fours are good, sixes are better: the next ball is a low full toss that Brook pings beautifully over backward square and into the crowd. An expensive over ends with a short ball that Brook wallops for four.
He and Root had to take their medicine at the start of their partnership, when it was tough to rotate strike never mind hit boundaries. It was worth it: they found their rhythm and have pillaged 111 from the last 12 overs.
36th over: England 228-2 (Root 69, Brook 75) Yawn, another milestone for Joe Root. He chips Wellalage over extra cover for four, then works two into the leg side to become the first England player to score 8000 ODI runs.
Root is suddenly all over Wellalage. He sweeps four more off the final ball of Wellalage's spell to move to 69 from 65 balls. That includes five brilliant boundaries from his last 13 balls. Unobtrusive, you say?
35th over: England 217-2 (Root 59, Brook 75) Root drags Malinga through backward square leg for four, an expertly placed stroke that was angled just enough to beat the man on the boundary. In their distinctive ways, Root and Brook are a life-affirming watch.
34th over: England 209-2 (Root 52, Brook 74) Respect my foot. Root races to his 49th ODI fifty with back-to-back boundaries off Wellalage. A jaunty reverse sweep prompted Wellalage to pull his length back, so Root clobbered another boundary over the leg side. It's been a typical, almost cliched Root innings: 54 balls, five fours, zero obtrusiveness.
A reminder that Root needs 64 today to become the first Englishman to make 8000 ODI runs. Oh, and he's averaging 109 in ODIs this year.
33rd over: England 198-2 (Root 43, Brook 72) Brook's ability and imagination are borderline offensive. He makes room to lift a slower short ball from Malinga over the fielder at short third and away for four.
A good over from Malinga includes the first suggestion of reverse swing. From memory, Sri Lanka used reverse swing very effectively when they beat England at Headingley last month.
32nd over: England 193-2 (Root 42, Brook 68) England continue to play Wellalage with nuff respect, taking three singles from his eighth over. Wellalage has outstanding figures of 8-0-34-2.
31st over: England 190-2 (Root 40, Brook 67) Breaking news: Harry Brook is on the rampage. He smokes Madushanka for 16 in three balls: a flash through backward point for four, a straight drive on the charge for four and a devastating back-foot slap down the ground for six.
Madushanka almost has the final word with a slower short ball that Brook top-edges fractionally short of the keeper. After a mini-orgy of 57 runs in six overs, it's time for drinks.
30th over: England 174-2 (Root 39, Brook 52) Sri Lanka reintroduce the left-arm spinner Wellalage, hoping the horse hasn't bolted. England are in a strong position, meaning Root and Brook can play low-risk cricket: two singles apiece.
29th over: England 170-2 (Root 37, Brook 50) Brook dabs Asitha for a single to reach a punishing fifty from 42 balls, including 37 runs from the 18. And it continues his superb form in ODIs since he took over from Jos Buttler.
Captain 1081 runs at 51.47; strike-rate 115; three hundreds, six fifties.
Not captain 504 runs at 25.20; SR 89; no hundreds, three fifties.
Root looks at his bat in confusion after mistiming a chip that only just clears midwicket.
(Edit: I forgot that those Brook stats include some games as stand-in captain in 2024. Since he took over full-time in 2025, he averages around 45 with a strike-rate of 111.)
28th over: England 167-2 (Root 35, Brook 49) Liyanage is hooked after conceding 16 from his first over. Shanaka replaces him and bowls a poor ball that Root touches off the hip for four. He is also starting to rotate strike again after a quiet few overs.
A brusque pull from Brook races through midwicket for four. The fielder on the boundary made a diving stop but was touching the sponge as he did so. England have scored 34 from the last three overs.
26th over: England 149-2 (Root 26, Brook 42) The new bowler Janith Liyanage is clattered down the ground for four by Brook, who then jumps across to scoop an extravagant six.
Brook has taken a short cut from first gear to fifth. After struggling to 13 not out from 24 balls, he has blistered 29 from the last 11. One day, when we're old and doddery, we'll realise how lucky we were to watch Joe Root and Harry Brook bat.
25th over: England 133-2 (Root 25, Brook 28) After a fast start, Root is struggling to rotate strike. It makes no sense, but the same thing against Pakistan on Tuesday. This has certainly been an innings of two halves: 20 from the first 15 balls, 5 from the last 15.
"Greetings from Barcelona!" says Gary Naylor. "I can't find a bar showing the cricket. Mind you, I suspect the same would be true in London #MakeCricketGreatAgain."
24th over: England 130-2 (Root 24, Brook 26) Something has given. Brook breaks the shackles by hitting consecutive balls from Kamindu Mendis for six. The first was an effortless drive over extra cover, the second a withering pull when Mendis pulled his length back. And with that, his strike rate jumps to 96.
23rd over: England 117-2 (Root 24, Brook 13) Brook fails to put away a full toss from Madushanka, then misses a dab outside off stump. Brook has a strike-rate of 57, and something is surely about to give.
22nd over: England 115-2 (Root 23, Brook 12) A change of left-arm spinner, with Kamindu Mendis on for Wellalage. Four from the over. It's a bit of a struggle for England just now, Brook in particular; he has 12 from 19 balls with no boundaries. What hell kinda Harry Brook innings is this?
21st over: England 111-2 (Root 22, Brook 9) The left-arm quick Madushanka returns. He goes round the wicket in an attempt to cramp the two right-handers, a tactic that works effectively to Root in that over.
Madushanka also has an unsuccessful LBW review when Root flicks across the line. The angle meant it was always going to miss leg stump, so Sri Lanka lose a review.
new_text:
Harry Brook hit a record-breaking 202 for England but still ended up on the losing side after Sri Lanka chased down 430 to win an incredible game by two wickets
49.5 overs: Sri Lanka 430-8 (Liyanage 61, Asitha Fernando 1), target 430. So what can Liyanage do under pressure - Tongue puts it tight in the slot ... and Liyanage sends it straight over everyone's head for a brutal six to win the game, and complete one of the greatest ODI run chases the game has ever seen. Harry Brook's heroics were in a losing cause.
And I'll leave you with Taha Hashim's report of a memorable, crazy, record-breaking, chastening/thrilling match. Thanks for following and emailing. Bye.
Harry Brook pulverised his way to the fastest double hundred in ODI history and it still was not enough for England. Sri Lanka were the victors in this absurd contest, hauling down a target of 430 in Rawalpindi, the second-highest successful chase in the history of the format. Only that magical 438 game, 20 years ago, trumps it.
Pavan Rathnayake, Dasun Shanaka and Avishka Fernando were the headliners, somehow turning it around for Sri Lanka after they were reduced to 24 for two. Rathnayake top-scored with 130, Fernando struck 97, and Shanaka - with 97 of his own - was the most brutal of the lot. After being taken apart with the ball, his revenge act included eight sixes. None of the trio were there at the close, as England suddenly found themselves back in it.
Up comes a crestfallen Harry Brook, who said his record-breaking knock now has "no value whatsoever" to him.
It was an incredible game of cricket - both teams were exceptional. Sri Lanka outplayed us unfortunately, we couldn't hit our straps with the ball, but fair play to them. [My own batting] was a nice innings - unfortunately it does not mean anything now. It has no value whatsoever in my eyes. We need to get together and go back to the drawing board a little bit. We know where we've gone wrong.
Kusal Mendis:
We've won the toss in our last five games and every game we've chased because of the dew. It was a very good game today; as a captain I really enjoyed it. Me and the coach talked to the players before the chase to play the first couple of overs as normal, then we decided Dasun [Shanaka] would come in earlier and everyone batted really well and took responsibility. Everyone showed their characters and belief in themselves.
This has been quite the cricketing week, with South Africa levelling the Test series against Australia. Here's Geoff Lemon:
It took time, it gently frayed nerves, but ultimately South Africa sealed the second Test at Gqeberha deep into the final day, clear by an innings and 31 runs, levelling the series with one to play. In truth, although Australia made 295 and got within 28 overs of safety, they did not deserve to save this game, even if Scott Boland and Travis Head did. Letting South Africa escape from 40 for four to pass 400 was the first offence, then came Australia's capitulation for 99 to be forced to follow on. The salvage operation was in waters too deep.
England face Pakistan next, on Sunday in Lahore, before Pakistan face Sri Lanka on Tuesday at the same venue, which also hosts the England-Sri Lanka rematch next Thursday. The final is on Sunday week in Lahore.
Sri Lanka pull off second highest ever successful ODI run chase
If England's batting brought almost unprecedented levels of brutal pyrotechnics, Sri Lanka's was an extraordinarily well paced and judged. Avishka Fernando and Rathnayeke laid the foundations for Shanakas and then Liyanage's extraordinary finishing.
Conditions were a batter's dream, for sure, but England did not bowl, looked bereft of cutting edge for long spells, and poor Sam Curran has conceded the most expensive ever figures by an England bowler in an ODI. Josh Tongue's excellent death bowling nearly won it before Liyanage held his nerve and won it.
49.5 overs: Sri Lanka 430-8 (Liyanage 61, Asitha Fernando 1), target 430. So what can Liyanage do under pressure - Tongue puts it tight in the slot ... and Liyanage sends it straight over everyone's head for a brutal six to win the game, and complete one of the greatest ODI run chases the game has ever seen. Harry Brook's heroics were in a losing cause.
49th over: Sri Lanka 422-6 (Liyanage 54, Wellalage 5), target 430. Overton returns, with a good ball speared in that Wellalage glides backward of square for one, but a misfield grants them two. The next, short-pitched one, cracks Wellalage on the grille. He's OK but it's a dot. A single follows. Nine needed. Liyanage swings and misses. Overton ends with one more single conceded.
48th over: Sri Lanka 417-6 (Liyanage 52, Wellalage 5), target 430. Jacks has been England's best bowler in these late stages and he begins with one, dot, one, before Liyanage straight drives for four to bring up a 21-ball 50. Magnificent stuff. A single follows before Wellalage ends the over with a straight drive over the bowler's head for four! Incredible. Thirteen needed off two.
47th over: Sri Lanka 406-6 (Liyanage 46), target 430. Carnage! A smart reverse scoop from Liyanage off Curran starts the over with a four. A square cut for four more follows - this is crazy. But not as crazy as the next shot, the purest of straight drives for SIX. A single follows. Arachchige's the new man in but he's unfazed, ramping over the keeper for four more - but the fun can't last as he sends a full toss next ball high to long on where it's pouched by Jacks. It's reviewed for a high ball but it's fine. He's out.
46th over: Sri Lanka 387-5 (Liyanage 31, Arachchige 9), target 430. We're over 800 runs for the match now, as Arachchige creams a lofted drive for four off Jacks, who is mostly pretty controlled, until one slips out of his hand for a beamer that is hack-edged to third man, with the boundary well saved. Jacks rounds off the over with a dot, a speared in yorker that confounds the battter's attempted reverse sweep.
45th over: Sri Lanka 377-5 (Liyanage 29, Arachchige 1), target 430. Liyanage drags Sri Lanka off the canvas straight away with consecutive fours off Overton, followed by a well run single. Sri Lanka's batting performance has been brilliantly indefatiguable it must be said. Arachchige nudges a single into a gap, before Liyanage drives the last ball of the over for four.
Wicket! Shanaka c Banton b Dawson 97, Sri Lanka 363-5
44th over: Sri Lanka 363-5 (Liyanage 16), target 430. Dawson starts his over by yielding two singles, before Liyanige sends a brilliant telegraphed reverse sweep over the infield for four. Better follows for Sri Lanka - an on-drive for SIX, then a single that brings to the strike Shanaka, who falls for 97 - his thumping drive taken at long-on by Banton again.
43rd over: Sri Lanka 350-4 (Shanaka 96, Liyanage 4), target 430. Shanaka ramps things up again as he pulls Curran into the crowd for his sixth SIX. A cut single follows, Liyanage drives for another, before Shanaka thumps the cleanest, most majestic SIX of his knock - right out of the screws, straight over the sightscreen. Curran's retort is a fine dot-ball yorker ... but Shanaka's retort to the retort is even better, pulled over square leg for SIX MORE.
42nd over: Sri Lanka 330-4 (Shanaka 77, Liyanage 3), target 430. Jacks is back at last, as the air begins to be sucked from this chase suddenly, and boundaries prove more elusive. It's really canny bowling from Jacks, offering little that's short and wide. Sri Lanka now need more than two a ball.
41st over: Sri Lanka 326-4 (Shanaka 74, Liyanage 2), target 430. A partnership of 133. is broken when Rathnayeke holes out, bringing the in-form Liyanage to the crease but he has no time to play himself in, and five from the over is not much use. 104 needed off 54 balls.
Wicket! Rathnayeke c Banton b Curran 130, Sri Lanka 323-4
No sooner do I say that than Rathnayeke perishes, tiredness getting to him, as he offers up a high on drive intoo Banton's hands on the boundary, for a career best score.
40th over: Sri Lanka 321-3 (Rathnayake 128, Shanaka 73), target 430. Tongue, after a superb early wicket, has struggled a touch today, and Rathnayake eases a long hop over backward point for four. Tongue gets a better length after that, until Shanaka swings inelegantly at a slower ball but its sliced over backward point and zips through for four.
Sri Lanka need 109 from 10 overs. If these two stay together, this is on.
39th over: Sri Lanka 309-3 (Rathnayake 120, Shanaka 67), target 430. Rathnayake takes two off an Atkinson full toss. The dew is beginning to take effect as Jacks sees a Rathnayake drive slide past him on the boundary for four, as SL advance to 300. This didn't seem on at 24 for 2. Shanaka celebrates it with the cleanest of straight hits for SIX. They're still favourites but England are really toiling here.
"The record breaking 200 may still go in vain," quips Krishna Moorthy.
38th over: Sri Lanka 292-3 (Rathnayake 113, Shanaka 60), target 430. Curran returns from the other end, and is creamed over extra cover for four by Shanaka - a yorker turned into a half-volley. Curran stems the tide, as so often, with a judicious slowie, but he can't stop Shanaka bringing up his 50 off 30 balls by sending another slower ball wide down leg to the deep square leg boundary. Nor can he stop Shanaka driving the next moon ball into the crowd for SIX to bring up the 100 partnership.
37th over: Sri Lanka 274-3 (Rathnayake 112, Shanaka 43), target 430. Brook continues to reshuffle his attack and brings back Overton for Curran. Rathnayake has found gaps well in this innings and sends an overpitched one outside off through the covers for four. Overton responds with a dot-ball bumper before a gloriously timed cut through backward point brings Rathnayake four more.
Sri Lanka remain ahead of England at this stage - but they don't have Harry Brook.
36th over: Sri Lanka 264-3 (Rathnayake 103, Shanaka 42), target 430. Dawson is brought back into the attack - where's Jacks? - and tucks the batters up nicely for three balls. Then, he snares Shanaka in front, sweeping and missing. The batter reviews, and successfully, as his front foot is outside the line. It's a good over from Dawson.
35th over: Sri Lanka 260-3 (Rathnayake 101, Shanaka 40), target 430. Rathnayake brings up a superb hundred in the circs with a controlled cut off Curran through point for two; it's his second ODI century, the other coming against England at the start of the year. Shanaka later adds to the party mood with a crack over deep point for SIX more.
34th over: Sri Lanka 251-3 (Rathnayake 98, Shanaka 33), target 430. Atkinson returns, with five of his overs still to bowl, and he thinks he's got his man straight off: Shanaka tries to pull a short one but grubs it behind where Cox takes a fine sprawling catch. The finger goes up but the batter reviews, reasoning it came off the helmet - which it did. Shanaka then gets away with a straight hack in the air which drops safely at midwicket. A misfield at deep backward square then grants Rathnayake four. The same shot next ball, more cleanly struck, bounces just short and is four more. Rathnayake adds two more to go within two of his ton.
33rd over: Sri Lanka 239-3 (Rathnayake 89, Shanaka 32), target 430. Sam Curran loves the slower ball and the moon ball but they still take batters by surprise and they can't work them away here in the first two balls of the over, but Shanaka responds with a pull round the corner for four - he's going at around two runs a ball. But Curran probably wins the battle for control and momentum from this particular over.
32nd over: Sri Lanka 234-3 (Rathnayake 88, Shanaka 27), target 430. Overton is held back and Dawson replaces him, and effectively initially, cramping up Shanaka until he manages to lift one over the offside infield for four. The next is even bigger, a crunching lofted on-drive for SIX. Less than 200 needed but it needs T20 level pyrotechnics now.
31st over: Sri Lanka 223-3 (Rathnayake 87, Shanaka 17), target 430. Curran is wisely reintroduced, and moonballs it up to the max first up for a dot ball before a well-run three from Shanaka's bat. But some composure returns from England's point of view - six from the over is not much use to Sri Lanka at this point.
30th over: Sri Lanka 217-3 (Rathnayake 85, Shanaka 13), target 430. Overton suddenly looks comfortably England's trickiest bowler - he has three to go after this one - and the batters are finding it much harder to work him away. A single and three dots are followed by a sumptuous gap-finding textbook square cut for four by Rathnayake.
29th over: Sri Lanka 212-3 (Rathnayake 81, Shanaka 12), target 430. Tongue's getting some treatment from Rathnayake, who swivel pulls into the crowd for another SIX - a fine statement that - as the 200 comes up. Another single ensues before Shanaka opens the face to send a controlled edge through the vacant slip area for four. Next ball, even better, a swing over square leg that just eludes Dawson on the boundary ... SIX more. Shanaka justifying his promotion instantly. That was the most expensive over of the innings.
28th over: Sri Lanka 194-3 (Rathnayake 74, Shanaka 1), target 430. Just as Sri Lanka dare to dream, Fernando perishes, Overton finding some sorely needed pace and bounce. Shanaka is promoted to No 5, and is off the mark with a single straight off. That extra pace and bounce also befuddles Cox behind the stumps, who fumbles his take and yields a bye.
Wicket! Avishka Fernando c and b Overton 97, Sri Lanka 190-3
Heartache for Avishka Fernando, who's flummoxed by a ball that climbs sharply at him, and he can only hack a return catch to the bowler. A big partnership ends.
27th over: Sri Lanka 190-2 (Avishka Fernando 97, Rathnayake 72), target 430. Tongue is brought back, and is rudely greeted by a lovely lofted square cut for four by Rathnayake, who improves on that next ball with an effortless pull for SIX off a short ball. A single brings to the strike Fernando, who inches closer to his 100 with a single. England struggling for a response here. Two dots to round off the over at least restore some control.
26th over: Sri Lanka 178-2 (Avishka Fernando 96, Rathnayake 61), target 430. Overton continues, and the batters help themselves to some singles, before Rathnayake cracks a lofted straight drive for four to bring up the 150 partnership in 130 balls.
25th over: Sri Lanka 169-2 (Avishka Fernando 94, Rathnayake 54), target 430. Fernando sizes up Dawson and absolutely belts him over long-on for a much needed SIX. At the hslfway stage Sri Lanka are kind of still in this.
24th over: Sri Lanka 159-2 (Avishka Fernando 86, Rathnayake 52), target 430. Has everyone just been watching South Africa v Australia during this middle-overs push and runfest? As if sensing that a global audience has just switched back, Fernando cracks Overton over his head for four. Next ball, Brook squanders a run-out chance after the batters get mixed up but makes the wrong decision with a wayward throw. He's had a busy day.
The teams are actually about level on run rate - at this stage.
23rd over: Sri Lanka 152-2 (Avishka Fernando 80, Rathnayake 51), target 430: Rathnayake drives for one to bring up a second consecutive 50, and it's been a composed one. The singles continue to be pushed but as we approach halfway Sri Lanka know they'll need to go on the charge at some point.
22nd over: Sri Lanka 144-2 (Avishka Fernando 74, Rathnayake 49), target 430: A deft reverse sweep off Jacks brings Rathnayake four more, then the singles and striker rotation continue. Batting continues to look easy, bowling a toothless chore. I know he's getting on and not in the best form, but England could do with a bit of Adil Rashid's magic here.
21st over: Sri Lanka 135-2 (Avishka Fernando 73, Rathnayake 41), target 430: Dawson switches ends, but there's not much turn in the pitch and little sense that spin will bring much beyond control at the moment. It's all very middle-overs like. Some singles happen and not much else.
20th over: Sri Lanka 131-2 (Avishka Fernando 71, Rathnayake 39), target 430: Will Jacks, who's already had some fun today, comes into the attack - and is thwacked square for four by Fernando; this has been a crucial knock by him on his return to the side. Singles are milked, and England still have work to do.
19th over: Sri Lanka 124-2 (Avishka Fernando 65, Rathnayake 38), target 430: Rathnayake drives Curran for two, then one, the bowler using his moonball at one point to maintain control, a control he loses with a long hop that Rathnayake clobbers for four through midwicket. Two more bring up the 100 partnership.
18th over: Sri Lanka 114-2 (Avishka Fernando 64, Rathnayake 29), target 430: Fernando pushes Dawson through the legside for one before ... Curran fluffs a catch on the boundary after a brutal high drive from Fernando, which appears to have gone through his hands. Four more, from Dawson's most expensive over thus far.
17th over: Sri Lanka 106-2 (Avishka Fernando 58, Rathnayake 27), target 430: Sam Curran replaces Overton as England seek to make something happen, as Fernando brings up his 50 with a nudged two through square leg. He and Sri Lanka need that - and they're keen on looseners down leg by Sam Curran too, and Fernando helps himself to four through the vacant deep fine leg area.
And that's drinks. Sri Lanka are still in this, with two set batters, but they'll need another gear change at some point, and may not have that in them.
16th over: Sri Lanka 97-2 (Avishka Fernando 49, Rathnayake 27), target 430: Dawson's doing OK here, offering some control albeit without looking like taking a wicket. But two from the over keeps England on top.
15th over: Sri Lanka 95-2 (Avishka Fernando 48, Rathnayake 26), target 430: Fernando, emboldened by this partnership's progress, swings Overton over deep midwicket for four to gee up a crowd that, to be fair, now looks bigger than it was earlier in the afternoon. Fernando helps another round the corner for four as England just lapse into the middle-overs rut to which they are sometimes prone.

I vividly recall standing at a bus stop in Orkney in the summer of 2018, listening to a Test Match Special podcast, when Michael Vaughan said there was a kid at Yorkshire who would play for England. I'd never heard of Harry Brook, but Vaughan spoke with such certainty that I made a point of following his career. In the next two seasons he averaged 25 and 21 in first-class cricket, and I thought Vaughany has sold us a pup. Wrong! 40th
